label: Realistic grant pack: four documents, two attachments missing, a legal-form name difference, a funding difference, a held ambiguous date and a genuine end-date difference (fictional)
preregistration: Written and committed BEFORE any model extraction on these documents (PC-T1). Expected findings follow from the seeded differences in tools/benchmark/src/realistic-packcheck.ts. The requirements list nine attachments; the form lists seven. "Tax clearance certificate" and "Bank confirmation letter" are not listed (Needs review while coverage is unverified; Confirmed if coverage is confirmed). "Letter of support" is listed for the requirement "Letters of support": that is only a SUGGESTED match (match scores are suggestions), so the requirement stays Needs review, with or without coverage. CORRECTION made before any inference: the first draft of this note called the singular/plural pair "not a difference"; an offline rule check on ideal extraction showed the rules, correctly by the project's own principle, keep it as Needs review, so the expectation was corrected here. The budget names the applicant without its legal form ("Riverbend Water Stewards" for "... NPC"): Needs review, not a confirmed difference. The form asks R2.4 million (written with a magnitude word) and the budget R 2 450 000: a confirmed difference. The budget period 01/04/2027 to 30/09/2028: the start date is ambiguous (day and month both 12 or less) and must be held for review, the end date is unambiguous and differs from the form (31 March 2028): confirmed. Total project budget R 3 150 000 is not below the funding requested: no budget finding. The registration certificate agrees with the form on the name. Distractors that are NOT the fields: award range R500 000 to R3 000 000, a previous grant of R450 000, closing date 15 December 2027, households served, budget lines, own contribution, registration date 12 June 2019. Labels are never read by extraction, chunking or matching.

lines: Grant call GC-2027: Community Water Resilience Fund (fictional sample)
This note sets out what an applicant must send together with its application form.
Applications close on 15 December 2027 and late applications are not read.
Awards range between R500 000 and R3 000 000 depending on the size of the project.
Who may apply
Registered non-profit organisations working on water supply in rural communities may apply.
An organisation may submit one application in each funding round.
Projects must be completed within eighteen months of the award.
What to attach
Every item below must be sent with the application. Documents are listed in the order they are read.
Required attachment: Application form
Required attachment: Project budget
Required attachment: Registration certificate
The registration certificate must show the legal name exactly as it appears on the application form.
Required attachment: Tax clearance certificate
Required attachment: Board resolution
Required attachment: Bank confirmation letter
Statements older than two years will not be accepted.
Required attachment: Annual financial statements
Required attachment: Project work plan
Required attachment: Letters of support
How applications are assessed
Each application is read by two assessors who score it against the published criteria.
Assessors look at need, value for money, community involvement and the strength of the plan.
The panel may ask an applicant to clarify any part of its application in writing.
Successful applicants are told by letter and the list of awards is published afterwards.
Funds are paid in three instalments linked to reports on progress.
The fund keeps the right to withdraw an award if information given turns out to be untrue.
Applicants should keep a copy of everything they send.
This note is invented for software testing only and describes no real grant.
Application form for grant GC-2027 (fictional sample)
Please complete every section in plain language.
Applicant details
Organisation name: Riverbend Water Stewards NPC
Contact person: the programme manager, whose details are in the covering letter.
Number of households served: 1 200
Previous grant received: R450 000 in 2025 for a smaller borehole project.
The project
Funding requested: R2.4 million
Project start date: 1 April 2027
Project end date: 31 March 2028
The project repairs and extends the water supply to six villages along the Riverbend valley.
Work includes rehabilitating boreholes, installing storage tanks and training local caretakers.
Villagers will help to choose tank sites and will take part in the monitoring each month.
We expect the supply to reach every household within the project period.
Progress reports will be sent at the end of each quarter.
Attachments provided with this form
Attachment provided: Application form
Attachment provided: Project budget
Attachment provided: Registration certificate
Attachment provided: Board resolution
Attachment provided: Annual financial statements
Attachment provided: Project work plan
Attachment provided: Letter of support
Declaration
I confirm that the information in this form is correct to the best of my knowledge.
I understand that an award may be withdrawn if any information given is found to be untrue.
The organisation has not applied to any other fund for the same costs.
Signed for the organisation by its authorised officer.
This form is invented for software testing only.
